name: Distinguish a witnessed event from belief and judgement

uses.action: Ask Kip where he stood and Otla who supplied the noun. The count, the inference and the later speaker occupy separate lines of the page.

name: Keep investigating while a question is open

uses.action: Test the chip with two fresh impressions. Keep the physical correspondence and leave the note’s signatory open for another witness.

name: Find a hidden assumption in a question

uses.action: Reconstruct the premise in the household rhyme. Two traced outlines fit one spoon and two lamps as well as two spoons and a middle lamp.

name: Check whether a claim fits what an observer can see

uses.action: Stand at the marked market corner. Follow the fold to the shaded hatch and mark where the line of sight to the hand breaks.

name: Separate a supportable reading from an added claim

uses.action: Trace the two edges and lift the sheet to date the handwritten name by its crease. The name and the edges have different sources.
Compare the same edge positions under light and chalk. A claim about equal brightness can be tested only with the lit view.
